steward_ingra.name: Ingra, Steward of Saltfell
lines_first: You'll be off a boat. You've got the walk. Sit down before you fall down.
I'm Ingra. I keep the stores and the hearth and most of the people in this house, whether they like it or not.
There's stew. You're not having any till you've washed, mind. Well's in the yard.
We're short a sack of rye. I've counted it four times. Somebody's dog has had it, and I know whose dog.
If you see it, you bring it back. I'll not have folk saying Saltfell can't feed a guest.
lines_repeat: Three nights you're household. After that you're either kin or gone, and you don't look like gone.
Gunna's up in the loft. Don't go up. She bites.
That end of the table's Brede's. He's particular about his end.

on_talk.toast: Ingra takes the rye. Received: Bog-iron ×1

lines: Eleven. Twelve. Eleven.
Sit down. You've been on your feet all day.
Found it in the byre, did you. Under that dog. Well. He's a good dog.
You've got a look of someone. Don't mind me. Everyone's got a look of someone.

services.label: Learn the Mending Song
services.line_done: Hum it over the cut, not at it. And don't look so pleased with yourself, everyone knows it.

services.label: Trade for a Deep Gourd
services.line_done: That was my mother's. It leaks if you hold it wrong. Don't hold it wrong.

services.label: Trade for a Deep Gourd
services.line_done: That was my mother's. It leaks if you hold it wrong. Don't hold it wrong.

brede.name: Brede
lines_first: Mind the oars. No, the other way. Thank you.
Brede. I'd shake your hand but I've had it in fish guts all afternoon.
Off to Kettle Fjord at first light. They've a healer there, a good one. There's a few coughing up at the house. Nothing much. Children, mostly.
Gunna says I'm not to go. Gunna says a lot of things. She's mending the big net, so she's not speaking to anyone anyway.
Lost my float off the herring net this morning. Cork, my knot burned on it. If the tide brings it in, I'd thank you for it. She'll notice it's gone and I'll never hear the end of it.
lines_repeat: Tide's right at first light. I'll be back before she's finished being cross.
Ever been to Kettle Fjord? They boil the fish in kettles the size of this boat. You can smell it a day out.
Don't tell Gunna I said she was cross.

lines: She does this faster. I don't know how she does it.
Pass us that. No. Yes. Thank you.
That's it. That's my knot. The one on the back's wrong, I did it the year we married. She says it makes it lucky.
You've done me a kindness. If you're ever in a boat, take the oilskins. I've another set.

services.label: Take Brede's spare oilskins
services.line_done: They've been in salt water more than I have. Keep 'em that way round.

services.label: Buy a lump of bog-iron
services.line_done: Raked it up for sinkers. You'll do better with it.

aud.name: Aud, barrow-keeper's widow
lines_first: Keep to the road, love. The turf's soft either side and I'm not pulling you out.
Aud. Orm kept these mounds forty years and I kept Orm, so I know them as well as he did. Better. He'd say so himself.
That's the Holms' lot. That's the miller's people, all eleven, and the miller still owes for three of them. That one's empty, whatever anyone tells you.
Orm's the last one on the road. I tie him a bit of heather every evening. He liked the purple. Bring me white and you can take it back.
His cord went in with him. Every burial on the hill, in knots. His brother wanted the knife put in. I won.
lines_repeat: Turf goes back the same day. That's the whole of the job. Orm made it sound harder.
Arne Holm cut every sod on this hill. You can tell his by the edge. Straight as a shelf.
His girls were up here this morning, the pair of them, stealing his spade. He let them.

lines: I've moved the heather. It was always that one. I don't know why you're looking at me like that.
Arne's sat out with his girls again. They'll be on about the window. They always are.
That's Orm's cord. He tied his knots too tight. You can't read a word of it, so don't try.
First on the road. It says a lot of things. He tied it in the dark half the time.
You'll want his other cloak. He was buried in the good one.

services.label: Learn the Turf-Laying Song
services.line_done: It's counting, mostly. Count with the spade, not ahead of it. Orm counted ahead of it.

services.label: Take Orm's working cloak
services.line_done: He was long in the arm. Turn the cuffs back. Don't cut them.

services.label: Sit on the wall with Aud

hesk.name: Hesk, travelling smith
lines_first: Don't stand there, you're in my draught. There. No. There.
Hesk. I do the coast twice a year, when the wind lets me. On the Lowe it never lets me.
Bog-iron. You rake it out of the black water and it comes up looking like something the dog left. Give it a day in here and it's a hinge.
Lost my good tongs in the bog this morning, raking. Went in to the elbow after them. I'm not going in to the shoulder for anyone's tongs, not even mine.
If you've iron, I'll put it in that blade. If you've not, sit out of the wind and don't touch anything.
lines_repeat: Wind's wrong again. It's always wrong on the Lowe.
Arne wants his spade edged before the Melt. I told him I'm a smith, not a miracle.
These are borrowed tongs. You can tell. They don't like me.

on_talk.toast: Hesk takes the tongs. Received: Bog-iron ×1

lines: Wind's come right. First time all summer. I don't trust it.
Fire's drawing like a chimney. Pass me that, quick, before it changes its mind.
Never that good, these. Bent in the rein. I'll have them back all the same.
Put your blade on the stone. I'll do it for less. Don't go telling people.

services.label: Fold bog-iron into the blade
services.line_done: There. It'll hold an edge now. Try not to use it on stones.
services.line_no_glass: No iron, no edge. Go and rake some. Mind the black water.
services.line_no_warmth: %d warmth for the fire. Peat doesn't cut itself.
services.line_max: There's no more iron going in that. It'd snap.

services.line_done: There. It'll hold an edge now. Try not to use it on stones.
services.line_no_glass: No iron, no edge. Go and rake some. Mind the black water.
services.line_no_warmth: %d warmth for the fire. Peat doesn't cut itself.
services.line_max: There's no more iron going in that. It'd snap.

services.label: Buy a lump of bog-iron
services.line_done: Last of what I raked before the tongs went in.

services.label: Buy the post maul
services.line_done: Drive posts with it. Or don't. It's yours, I'm not asking.

ivo.name: Ivo
lines_first: Hold that one. Not by the collar, she bites.
Grandfather says the ice isn't made yet. It's made. I walked on it this morning, out past the houses.
The healer's across at the far landing. Somebody's got to fetch her. Everybody keeps saying somebody.
Lost a mitten in the dog-pen. This one's Grandfather's. Don't tell him, he'll have me looking for it till dark.
lines_repeat: I'm not going anywhere. That's what he said to say.
The dogs know the way. The dogs always know the way.
He's put my supper on. I'll eat it when I'm back. When I'm back from the pen, I mean.

lines: That's mine. Where was it? I had it this morning.
There. Both my own. You can give Grandfather his back, I'm not going near him.
Fish again. He only knows the one way. You'd think in sixty years.

halla.name: Halla, trader
lines_first: If you're buying, I've salt, needles and a little iron. If you're selling, I've no room.
Halla. That's my boat, and that's my cord, and every knot on it's mine.
Sold the whole catch to the Tarnhall people for their feast. Forty barrels. They'll be eating it till the Melt.
We go on the morning tide. Sten'll be better at sea. It's the land air that's doing it.
lines_repeat: Forty barrels off, forty barrels paid for. I like a week like that.
Don't mind Sten. He's always been a cougher.

lines: I've put him in the end house by the fire. He can come down on the next boat. There's always a next boat.
That's not my knot. I don't tie it like that. One man, sick.
Sten. Come here. No, stay there. Stay there.

services.label: Buy a lump of iron
services.line_done: Southern iron. Better than your bog stuff. Don't tell your smith.

services.label: Buy a sealing harpoon
services.line_done: Took it off a sealer in a bad year for him. Line's new. Mostly.

services.label: Trade for a stoppered flask
services.line_done: Keep the cork in. That's all the advice you get for free.

sten.name: Sten, Halla's crewman
lines_first: Sorry. Don't mind me. It's the crossing, it gets in your chest.
Sten. I row for Halla. When she lets me. She says I cough out of time.
We'll be gone in the morning. Nobody here needs to catch anything off me.
I'd shake your hand. Best not.
lines_repeat: Sorry.
It's nothing. It's the crossing.
Hot in here, isn't it. Is it just me.

services.label: Take Sten's fur coat
services.line_done: Have it. I'm roasting. Don't let her see, it's on the cargo cord.
